page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1ne.8xlarge is an instance type belonging to the big data storage-dense family, deployed on the KVM hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 32 dedicated vCPUs driven by the Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor architecture at a base clock frequency of 2.5 GHz. Backing this compute layer is 128 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory distribution of 4.0 GB of RAM per virtual core. Network throughput is provisioned with a 20 Gbps baseline bandwidth, while complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

A primary architectural feature of the ecs.d1ne.8xlarge is its bundled local storage array, offering 94489 GB of local hard disk drive (HDD) capacity. This extreme local disk volume delivers massive raw storage density directly attached to the host, eliminating external network storage overhead for data retrieval. However, relying on rotational magnetic media presents architectural tradeoffs: random read and write latency, as well as total IOPS capability, are significantly lower compared to solid-state or NVMe-based flash arrays. The configuration is optimized for high-throughput sequential data patterns rather than transactional random access.

From an infrastructure cost perspective, the instance maximizes byte-per-core capacity, serving scenarios where maintaining voluminous datasets on flash drives is economically impractical. The older Broadwell-era Intel Xeon microarchitecture balances baseline multi-core execution with low resource costs across massive capacity footprints. Workload fit includes distributed big data analytics architectures, such as Apache Hadoop clusters, distributed MapReduce tasks, large-scale sequential extract-transform-load (ETL) pipelines, log archiving, and data lake storage processing where massive sequential disk capacity is required alongside 32 dedicated compute threads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1ne.8xlarge is a dedicated big data compute instance featuring 32 vCPUs powered by 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processors and 128 GB of RAM, adhering to a 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio. Built on the KVM hypervisor, this server integrates 94489 GB of local HDD storage and provides a 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system architecture emphasizes dense local capacity over low-latency random access, trading the high IOPS of NVMe drives for economical multi-terabyte sequential disk access. Operating without hardware GPU acceleration, the hardware balance suits high-volume distributed data processing frameworks, bulk log ingestion, data lake infrastructure, and sequential batch extract-transform-load jobs.
